prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want a specific name(s) or help finding one and vetting them? A couple quick questions will let me give much better recommendations:
- What kind of project? (kitchen, bath, whole‑house remodel, deck, roof, plumbing/electrical repair, etc.)
- Rough budget and desired start date?
- Any preferences (licensed trades only, insured/bonded, design-build, union, Green products, etc.)?

While you answer, here are practical, reliable ways to find and vet contractors in Joplin, plus things to look for and red flags to avoid.

Where to look (local & credible sources)
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce membership list — local reputable businesses often participate.
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — check ratings and complaints.
- Google Business listings, Yelp, Angi (formerly Angie’s List) and Houzz — for photos, reviews, and project galleries.
- Nextdoor and local Facebook groups — for neighborhood references.
- Local building supply stores (e.g., lumberyards) — staff often know reputable contractors.
- City of Joplin Building Division — they can tell you who pulls permits and if a contractor has had code issues.

Licenses and permits
- Confirm the contractor carries general liability insurance and workers’ compensation.
- For trade work (electrical, plumbing, HVAC), verify state or local licensing through Missouri resources and ask for license numbers and proof.
- Confirm who will obtain required permits (most reputable contractors handle permits and inspections).

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?
- How long have you been in business in the Joplin area?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references with phone numbers?
- Do you have photos of completed projects similar to mine?
- What is the estimated start date and timeline?
- What is the payment schedule and total cost breakdown?
- Who will manage the project day‑to‑day? Will subcontractors be used?
- How are change orders handled? What warranty do you provide?

What to require in writing
- A detailed written estimate/contract describing scope, materials, brand names, timeline, payment schedule, cleanup, and warranty.
- A written change‑order process and cost estimate for any additional work.
- Proof of insurance and copies of subcontractor insurance where applicable.
- A lien waiver clause (and obtain signed lien releases as you make payments).

Red flags
- Contractor asks for large upfront cash payment (more than 10–30% is risky).
- No written contract or unwillingness to sign detailed terms.
- Poor or no references, no local portfolio or unverified online reviews.
- Pressures you to make quick decisions or uses high‑pressure sales tactics.
- No business address, or only a cell phone and email.

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email/template RFP you can send to contractors.
- Create a short checklist to use during contractor interviews and reference checks.
- Provide a curated (non‑real‑time) list of types of local firms to contact (e.g., kitchen remodelers, general contractors, roofers) if you tell me the project type.

Which would you prefer?
